```plato
    //==
    // # Uniform, normal, and exponential bodies
    //
    // The `IProbabilityDistribution` obligations for the four elementary continuous
    // families of `random.types.plato`: UniformDistribution,
    // NormalDistribution, LogNormalDistribution and ExponentialDistribution. Every
    // Pdf and Mean here is exact; the Cdf of the two normal forms inherits the
    // 7.5e-8 error bound of `StandardNormalCdf` in the shared helpers above.

    //==
    // # UniformDistribution
    //
    // Parameterization: continuous uniform on the CLOSED interval [Min, Max].
    // Precondition: Min < Max (the degenerate Min == Max case divides by zero).
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continuous_uniform_distribution

    // The midpoint of the interval: (Min + Max) / 2.
    Mean(self: UniformDistribution): Number
        => (self.Min + self.Max) / 2.0;
```

```plato
    //==
    // # LogNormalDistribution
    //
    // Parameterization: LogMean (mu) and LogStandardDeviation (sigma) are the
    // mean and STANDARD DEVIATION OF THE UNDERLYING NORMAL, i.e. of ln(X), not
    // of X. Support is x > 0. Precondition: LogStandardDeviation > 0.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Log-normal_distribution

    // The mean of the variable itself: exp(mu + sigma^2 / 2).
    Mean(self: LogNormalDistribution): Number
        => (self.LogMean + self.LogStandardDeviation.Square / 2.0).Exp;
```

```plato
    //==
    // # ExponentialDistribution
    //
    // Parameterization: RATE (lambda), not scale — the mean is 1 / Rate.
    // Support is x >= 0. Precondition: Rate > 0.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exponential_distribution

    // The mean waiting time: the reciprocal of the rate.
    Mean(self: ExponentialDistribution): Number
        => 1.0 / self.Rate;
```

```plato
    //==
    // # Gamma- and beta-family bodies
    //
    // The `IProbabilityDistribution` obligations for GammaDistribution,
    // BetaDistribution, ChiSquaredDistribution and StudentTDistribution. These four
    // share one shape: their Mean and Variance are elementary closed forms, while
    // every Pdf and Cdf goes through the special-function vocabulary of the
    // `numbers.library.plato` — `Gamma`/`LogGamma`, `Beta`, and the
    // regularized incomplete forms `RegularizedGammaP` and `RegularizedBeta`.
    // The accuracy of each body is bounded by the accuracy stated on those
    // functions (roughly 1e-12 relative on their primary domains).

    //==
    // # GammaDistribution
    //
    // Parameterization: SHAPE (k) and SCALE (theta) — theta is a scale, NOT a
    // rate; the rate form uses beta = 1 / theta. Support is x > 0.
    // Precondition: Shape > 0 and Scale > 0.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamma_distribution

    // The mean: Shape * Scale.
    Mean(self: GammaDistribution): Number
        => self.Shape * self.Scale;
```

```plato
    //==
    // # BetaDistribution
    //
    // Parameterization: shape parameters Alpha and Beta, support the closed
    // interval [0, 1]. Precondition: Alpha > 0 and Beta > 0.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beta_distribution

    // The mean: Alpha / (Alpha + Beta).
    Mean(self: BetaDistribution): Number
```

```plato
    // # StudentTDistribution
    //
    // Parameterization: DegreesOfFreedom (nu), location 0 and scale 1 (this is
    // the standard, non-shifted t). Support is the whole real line.
    // Precondition: DegreesOfFreedom > 0.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Student%27s_t-distribution

    // The mean: 0 by symmetry. Precondition: DegreesOfFreedom > 1 — the mean is
    // undefined at or below one degree of freedom, where this reports 0 anyway.
    Mean(self: StudentTDistribution): Number
        => 0.0;
```

```plato
    //==
    // # Heavy-tailed, lifetime, and shaped distribution bodies
    //
    // The `IProbabilityDistribution` obligations for the remaining continuous
    // families of `random.types.plato`: the heavy-tailed CauchyDistribution
    // and the peaked LaplaceDistribution, the lifetime and power-law
    // WeibullDistribution and ParetoDistribution, the bounded
    // TriangularDistribution, and the circular VonMisesDistribution. All bodies
    // here are exact closed forms except the von Mises CDF (which has no closed
    // form and is a truncated Bessel series; see its site); the Weibull moments
    // and the von Mises bodies go through `Gamma` and the modified Bessel
    // functions `BesselI0`/`BesselI1` of `numbers.library.plato`, so
    // their accuracy is bounded by the accuracy stated on those functions.

    //==
    // # CauchyDistribution
    //
    // Parameterization: Location (x0, the median and mode) and Scale (gamma,
    // the half width at half maximum) — Scale is NOT a standard deviation; the
    // Cauchy distribution has none. Precondition: Scale > 0.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cauchy_distribution

    // The mean is undefined (the defining integral does not converge). By the
    // convention stated on the type, this reports the Location, which is the
    // median and mode.
    Mean(self: CauchyDistribution): Number
        => self.Location;
```

```plato
    // Parameterization: Location (mu, the mean/median/mode) and Scale (b, the

    Mean(self: LaplaceDistribution): Number
```

```plato
    //==
    // # WeibullDistribution
    //
    // Parameterization: SHAPE (k) and SCALE (lambda) — the two-parameter
    // Weibull with location 0, support x >= 0. Precondition: Shape > 0 and
    // Scale > 0.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weibull_distribution

    // The mean: lambda * Gamma(1 + 1/k).
    Mean(self: WeibullDistribution): Number
        => self.Scale * Gamma(1.0 + 1.0 / self.Shape);
```

```plato
    //==
    // # ParetoDistribution
    //
    // Parameterization: MinimumValue (x_m, the scale and the lower bound of the
    // support) and Shape (alpha, the tail index) — the Pareto Type I. Support is
    // x >= MinimumValue. Precondition: MinimumValue > 0 and Shape > 0.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pareto_distribution

    // The mean: alpha * x_m / (alpha - 1). Precondition: Shape > 1 — the mean is
    // infinite for Shape <= 1, where this expression is not meaningful.
    Mean(self: ParetoDistribution): Number
        => self.Shape * self.MinimumValue / (self.Shape - 1.0);
```

```plato
    //==
    // # TriangularDistribution
    //
    // Parameterization: lower limit Min (a), mode c, upper limit Max (b), with
    // support the closed interval [a, b]. Precondition: a <= c <= b and a < b.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triangular_distribution

    // The mean: (a + c + b) / 3.
    Mean(self: TriangularDistribution): Number
        => (self.Min + self.Mode + self.Max) / 3.0;
```

```plato
    //==
    // # Discrete distribution bodies
    //
    // The `IProbabilityDistribution` obligations for the types of
    // `random.types.plato`. Pdf reads the probability mass at the value rounded
    // down to a whole number, per that file's convention. The Binomial and Poisson
    // CDFs sum the masses directly — exact in form and O(k) — because their closed
    // forms are regularized incomplete beta and gamma functions, which this tree
    // cannot express. Factorial and BinomialCoefficient come from the shared
    // helpers at the top of this library.

    //==
    // # BernoulliDistribution
    //
    // Parameterization: SuccessProbability (p) in [0, 1]. Support is {0, 1};
    // per the section note above, Pdf reads the mass at the value rounded down.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernoulli_distribution

    // The mean: the success probability.
    Mean(self: BernoulliDistribution): Number
        => self.SuccessProbability.Value;
```

```plato
    //==
    // # BinomialDistribution
    //
    // Parameterization: TrialCount (n) independent trials each succeeding with
    // SuccessProbability (p). Support is the whole numbers 0..n; Pdf reads the
    // mass at the value rounded down. Precondition: TrialCount >= 0.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Binomial_distribution

    // The mean: n * p.
    Mean(self: BinomialDistribution): Number
        => self.TrialCount.ToNumber * self.SuccessProbability.Value;
```

```plato
    //==
    // # GeometricDistribution
    //
    // Parameterization: the number of FAILURES BEFORE the first success, so the
    // support is {0, 1, 2, ...} — NOT the "number of trials" variant supported
    // on {1, 2, ...}, which has mean 1/p. This matches the type's doc comment.
    // Precondition: SuccessProbability > 0.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geometric_distribution

    // The mean number of failures before the first success: (1 - p) / p.
    Mean(self: GeometricDistribution): Number
        => (1.0 - self.SuccessProbability.Value) / self.SuccessProbability.Value;
```

```plato
    // The mean outcome index: the weight-weighted average of 0..Count-1.
    Mean(self: DiscreteDistribution): Number
        => self.Weights.Count.Range
            .Map(i => i.ToNumber * self.Weights[i])
            .Reduce(0.0, (total, term) => total + term)
         / self.TotalWeight;
```
